raw_response:
The honest answer is: A is mostly ill-posed as a bridge test, unless it is demoted to a negative-control audit. The bridge is now correctly bio-gated.
The reason is that the “first-order” result on the codon side and any “spectral order” result on the Window6 side live in different harmonic geometries.
On the codon side,  $E_1$  is not just “low-frequency” in a vague sense. It is specifically the additive subspace of the Hamming association scheme  $H(3,4)=V_4^3$ :

$$E_1 = \text{functions depending additively on one codon position at a time}.$$

Because  $V_4$  is realized by the three chemical characters  $\chi_R,\chi_W,\chi_K$ , this  $E_1$  has a real biological interpretation: position-wise chemical dichotomies. The certified localization to position 3 and position 1, and to weak/strong plus purine/pyrimidine, says the bio residual is basically single-position base-chemistry structure.
Window6, however, is a different object: a 21-vertex induced subgraph of the Boolean cube  $Q_6$ , or equivalently the no-adjacent-1 language of length 6. Its canonical spectrum is either:


the Boolean Fourier spectrum of its indicator inside  $\{0,1\}^6$ , or


the adjacency/Laplacian spectrum of the Fibonacci cube  $\Gamma_6$ .


Neither is the same frame as the Krawtchouk decomposition of  $H(3,4)$ . To compare them, you must choose a map from six Boolean coordinates to three  $V_4$  codon positions, for example grouping bits as  $(1,2),(3,4),(5,6)$ . But that grouping is not forced by Window6 itself. It is imported from the codon side. Once you do that, any “Window6 is first-order/additive like codons” claim becomes vulnerable to the exact circularity the program has been trying to avoid.
There is a pure-math thing you can compute:
Let

$$f_W=\mathbf{1}_{X_6}-21/64$$

on the Boolean cube  $Q_6$ , where  $X_6$  is the no-adjacent-1 Window6 set. Compute its Boolean Fourier degree energies

$$\rho_k(W)=\frac{\sum_{|S|=k}\hat f_W(S)^2}{\sum_{S\ne\varnothing}\hat f_W(S)^2}.$$

Then test against all 21-subsets of  $Q_6$ , or better against all 21-subsets with the same edge count and maybe the same coordinate-weight distribution. This would tell you whether Window6 itself is first-order dominated, pairwise dominated, or high-order dominated as a Boolean object.
But that result would not bridge to codon  $E_1$ , because Boolean degree-1 in  $Q_6$  is not codon-position  $E_1$  in  $V_4^3$ . If you group Boolean bits into three pairs and then compute the  $H(3,4)$ -style  $E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3$  energy of the Window6 indicator under that grouping, the statistic becomes grouping-dependent. You would need to test across all 15 pairings of six bits into three unordered pairs, and probably all bit relabelings and flips. If the result only appears under the codon-like pairing, it is circular. If it appears under all pairings, it is probably a generic property of the no-adjacent constraint or size/edge profile, not a specific bridge.
So the strongest admissible version of A would be only this:
Object: Window6 indicator  $f_W=\mathbf{1}_{X_6}-21/64$  on  $Q_6$ .
Statistic: Boolean Fourier degree profile  $(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_6)$ , plus, as a secondary audit, the distribution of  $V_4^3$ -style  $E_1$  energy over all 15 pairings of Boolean coordinates into three  $V_4$  positions.
Null: all 21-subsets of  $Q_6$  matched for edge count 38 and coordinate-weight profile, or a stricter null preserving the no-adjacent language’s one-coordinate marginals and edge count.
Certification criterion: Window6 must show an algebraically extreme degree profile under that null, and the  $V_4^3$ -style first-order energy must be pairing-invariant rather than dependent on a codon-like pairing.
Likely outcome: even if extreme, it certifies a property of Window6, not a bridge to codon  $E_1$ . If the comparison requires choosing a special 6-bit to 3-position map, it is not non-circular.
That means A is not a good bridge step. At best it is a negative-control sanity check: does Window6 have its own low-order or high-order spectral character? It cannot rescue the failed  $E_3$  redirect, and it cannot convert the bio  $E_1$  finding into a Window6/Fibonacci forcing result without an independently justified common carrier.
The important conceptual shift is this:
The bio residual being  $E_1$ -dominated is not a hidden Fibonacci signature. It is almost the opposite. It says the residual lives where ordinary codon chemistry lives: single-position base pairing, especially wobble and position-1 cross-box structure. That is biologically plausible, but mathematically it is not the exotic highest-frequency layer. It weakens the Window6 spectral-bridge ambition.
So the honest verdict is:
bridge is correctly bio-gated; the decisive next input is an expanded cross-organism  $d_{\rm resid4}$  matrix.
There is no remaining pure-math/public-data step that can non-vacuously connect the certified bio  $E_1$  residual back to Window6 without importing a map that the previous non-q6 embedding failures have already warned against.
The remaining useful actions are empirical, not structural:


enlarge the organism panel;


test whether the  $E_1$  residual is stable across held-out clades;


determine whether the wobble/position-1 chemical axis survives tRNA-tAI, TE, organism, and expression controls;


ask whether it predicts an independent biological readout.


If that expanded gate fails, the spectral direction’s final result is still valuable but bounded:
the codon residual basis is first-order additive chemistry, not Window6/Fibonacci structure.
The sharpest next question is: In an expanded held-out organism panel, does the certified  $E_1$  wobble/position-1 residual remain a reproducible biological axis after tRNA-tAI, TE, and clade controls, or is it only a codon-spelling/composition artifact?
